rubric.why: This identifies metabolism as the totality of chemical reactions in an organism that sustain life.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that metabolism is the sum of chemical reactions in an organism that sustain life; equivalent wording is acceptable.

rubric.why: This distinguishes catabolism from anabolism by their direction of change and energy effect.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for including both catabolism (breaking complex molecules into simpler ones and releasing energy) and anabolism (building complex molecules from simpler ones and consuming energy).

modelAnswer: Metabolism is the sum of all chemical reactions that occur within an organism to sustain life. Catabolism involves the breakdown of complex molecules into simpler ones, releasing energy in the process. Anabolism involves building up complex molecules from simpler ones. This process consumes energy.

rubric.why: A biological catalyst is the defining term for an enzyme.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying an enzyme as a biological catalyst.

rubric.why: The role of an enzyme is to speed up reactions without being used up.
rubric.description: State the enzyme's role in metabolism.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that enzymes speed up reactions and are not consumed in the process.

modelAnswer: Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed up chemical reactions in living organisms without being consumed in the process. They are primarily proteins and are highly specific to their substrates (the molecules that undergo enzyme-controlled reactions).

rubric.why: The active site is described as a pocket or cleft on the enzyme's surface.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as a pocket or cleft on the enzyme surface called the active site.

rubric.why: The supplied answer states that active sites are directly involved in catalysis.
rubric.description: State the importance of the active site.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the active site is directly involved in catalysis.

modelAnswer: An enzyme has one or more pockets or clefts on its surface. These are called active sites. The active sites are directly involved in catalysis.

rubric.why: Increasing substrate concentration initially increases the reaction rate.
rubric.description: State the effect of increasing substrate concentration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an increase in substrate concentration increases the reaction rate.

rubric.why: At saturation, active sites are occupied and further substrate does not increase the reaction rate.
rubric.description: Explain the effect at high substrate concentration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that active sites become occupied (saturated), so further substrate does not increase the reaction rate.

modelAnswer: An increase in substrate concentration increases the rate of reaction. At high substrate concentration, all active sites of the enzymes are occupied. In this condition, any more substrate molecules do not find free active sites. This state is called saturation of active sites and reaction rate does not increase.

rubric.why: Pepsin is the example that works in the acidic conditions of the stomach.
rubric.description: Give one enzyme and its optimum conditions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying pepsin as working in an acidic medium in the stomach, with pH 1.5 to 2.0.

rubric.why: Trypsin is the example that works in alkaline conditions in the small intestine.
rubric.description: Give the second enzyme and its optimum conditions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying trypsin as working in an alkaline medium in the small intestine, with pH 7 to 8.

modelAnswer: For example, pepsin in stomach works in acidic medium (pH 1.5 to 2.0) while trypsin in small intestine works in alkaline medium (pH 7 to 8).

rubric.why: Optimum temperature is the specific temperature at which an enzyme works at its maximum rate.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an enzyme works at maximum rate at a specific temperature called its optimum temperature.

rubric.why: Optimum pH is the specific pH at which an enzyme shows maximum activity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an enzyme shows maximum activity at a specific pH called its optimum pH.

modelAnswer: Each enzyme works at maximum rate at a specific temperature called optimum temperature. They show maximum activity at a specific pH, called their optimum pH.

rubric.why: The identifying feature in the answer is that these inhibitors do not attach to the active site.
rubric.description: Identify the inhibitor type by its active-site binding.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying non-competitive inhibitors, or describing inhibitors that do not attach to the active site.

rubric.why: The answer describes inhibitors with no substrate similarity that attach at another enzyme location.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the inhibitor attaches to another location on the enzyme rather than the active site.

modelAnswer: Some enzyme inhibitors do not have similarity to the substrate. They do not attach to the active site of enzyme. Rather, they attach to some other location of enzyme.

rubric.why: Competitive inhibitors resemble the substrate and compete for the enzyme's active site.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that competitive inhibitors resemble the substrate and compete with it to attach to the active site.

rubric.why: Non-competitive inhibitors do not resemble the substrate or bind at the active site; they attach elsewhere.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that these inhibitors do not resemble the substrate and attach to another location on the enzyme, not the active site.

modelAnswer: Some inhibitors resemble the enzyme’s substrate. They compete with the substrate to attach to the active site of enzyme. Some enzyme inhibitors do not have similarity to the substrate. They do not attach to the active site of enzyme. Rather, they attach to some other location of enzyme.
